feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the header and experience strongly align around digital strategy, communications leadership, and platform modernization.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good specificity: tools, platforms, audience scale, and website size add substance and make claims believable.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes; include measurable impact such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, conversion improvements, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter structure.  
- Fix consistency/style issues: use “12 years of experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); consider consistent date style (“Oct.”/“Sept.”), and “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding mission-driven digital leadership will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more concrete positioning tied to digital transformation, governance, and content operations.
- Emphasize current value: leading cross-channel strategy, modernizing platforms, and building scalable systems for advocacy/public-sector organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and content operations, with a strong track record of building scalable workflows, improving governance, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep it here only if targeting advocacy-focused roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow; suggested rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS administration & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy, advocacy & public-sector communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Use “communications” instead of “communication” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider prioritizing the most recent/relevant strengths first: strategy, web/CMS, analytics, governance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills sections.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the header, competencies, and project section. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs and reduce generic phrasing like “support” and “advise.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or stakeholder groups served.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing toolkits; improved publishing consistency through stronger workflows, governance, and analytics.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” substantially overlaps with Recent Projects; keep one concise mention here and let the project section carry the technical detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language also echoes the header and NACo role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform and scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the highest-impact achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements for email/social/video if available.
- Tighten the remaining bullets to emphasize executive-level systems work: analytics stack expansion, governance standards, cross-department planning, and launch of the in-house broadcast studio.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on strategy, scale, and management.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as building enterprise production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the larger platform/governance work in the next role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution as a build-stage achievement: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by aligning communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent content coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid “strengthened workflows/governance” language that repeats the Director role.
- Avoid “weekly video updates” phrasing if the earlier 2015–2018 role already claims that same program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior, recent strengths and make the phrasing more distinctive and outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want closer alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale by referencing enterprise publishing, large web estates, or high-volume public communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat detailed software lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw tool list to a capability-led summary tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership, CMS modernization, front-end implementation, API/integration workflows, automation systems, AI-enabled search.”
- Cut lower-priority or older items here if they already appear elsewhere, especially “jQuery” and possibly “WordPress,” unless central to target roles.
- Group related skills for concision: “Drupal, SharePoint & Power Pages” or “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” rather than listing every item separately.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • HTML, CSS and JavaScript • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one place unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a senior, outcome-oriented capability summary. This section should emphasize strategic use of analytics, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, performance analysis and optimization”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for more standard phrasing.
- Add one higher-value capability if accurate: “Measurement frameworks” or “Dashboard development” to show strategic ownership.
- Keep only the most relevant tools here; move full platform inventory to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; avoid repeating the same tool list in both places.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so this should add specificity, not restate it.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple work-experience bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Studio, Video & Live Event Production”
- Tighten and elevate the list: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations • Run-of-show and technical production”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming and recurring event coverage”
- Consider replacing “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production” to better match Director-level experience

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already implied by NACo experience, so keep this section concise rather than repeating detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms or removed to reduce repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by demonstrated recent depth: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If keeping this section, add light proficiency framing: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider trimming lower-signal tools if space is tight: keep only platforms supported by recent work, especially Drupal and WordPress.
- If you want more impact, rename to “CMS & Web Platforms” and align wording with enterprise scope rather than listing tools only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes the same platforms plus modernization context.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel junior/lightweight compared with the enterprise emphasis elsewhere unless it supports a specific project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add specificity where credible: “Technical integrations: REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager”
- Keep newer, differentiating tools last: “Serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If space allows, group by function rather than listing flat keywords; this reads as more senior and less like a junior coding inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; consider removing them from one section or shortening this item to only the tools not named elsewhere.
- If GTM is central, consider moving it under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” to align with the analytics-heavy experience.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Integration & Work Management
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana
- Move general collaboration tools out unless central to workflow design: Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Drop lower-value or older/project-management-only tools if space is tight: Basecamp • Trello

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; keep this section tool-specific rather than repeating the same concept.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals; listing all four can read as padding unless each was materially used recently.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare to show level of ownership or fit with your recent leadership in email operations. It should read as enterprise engagement platforms, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/level to signal stronger capability: **Enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider ordering by recency/strength rather than brand recognition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in multiple NACo roles; keep this as tools only and leave audience scale/operational impact in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” is broad; avoid implying CRM/community management depth unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic verbs: replace “supporting the creation” and “strengthening workflows” with specific actions like “built,” “standardized,” “launched,” or “produced.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, email/social volume, or team support.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/editorial coordination language already used in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, cross-functional coordination, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with sharper language such as “produced multimedia and digital content supporting organizational programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audiences reached, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content expanded communications capacity.
- Keep this entry concise—1–2 lines max—since later NACo roles show the larger digital leadership progression.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating general multimedia/video language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize digital operations here; save that narrative for the 2015–2024 positions.
